name: Valkey Coordination Kernel — Conductor Model
description: Implement the Conductor Model: Valkey serializes coordination without serializing execution. Stream-based work queues with consumer groups, sorted-set priority scheduling and due-time wheels, TTL-based heartbeats and leases, and pub/sub for volatile UI only. Primitive implementation is substantially complete. The remaining gate is durable authority binding: every work lifecycle transition must be backed by observable PGlite state before Valkey ACK.
purpose: Replace all ad-hoc coordination (setTimeout, in-process locks, custom queues) with a single Valkey coordination spine where every authority-changing event flows through Valkey in order while expensive work runs in parallel workers. The mission closes only when the system proves the full lifecycle: create work in PGlite, enqueue to Valkey, consume through a group, record attempt start, record terminal/retry/dead-letter transition in PGlite, then ack.
acceptanceCriteria: Agent work queues using Valkey Streams with consumer groups prevent duplicate work
Every completeAndAck writes terminal durable state to PGlite before XACK
Every failRetryableAndAck writes retry-scheduled durable state to PGlite before requeue
Every deadLetterAndAck writes dead-letter durable record to PGlite before terminal XACK
reconcilePending inspects PGlite lifecycle state — never blind-ACKs to avoid blocking
Community support queue uses sorted sets with dharma-weighted priority scoring
Due-time wheel using sorted sets replaces all setTimeout/setInterval/cron
TTL heartbeat keys detect stale agents within 30 seconds
TTL lease keys ensure exclusive work ownership with expiry recovery
Pub/sub limited to volatile UI signals only — never for durable events
Tests inspect both PGlite and Valkey state for every lifecycle assertion
